thingsToDo.title: Sponge Docks
thingsToDo.description: Walk Dodecanese Boulevard for sponge-diving history, Greek restaurants, boats, shops, and the working Anclote River waterfront.

thingsToDo.title: Historic Downtown Tarpon Springs
thingsToDo.description: Explore the older commercial district for architecture, local businesses, cultural institutions, and a quieter counterpart to the Sponge Docks.

thingsToDo.title: Fred Howard Park
thingsToDo.description: Use the causeway and Gulf beach for swimming, paddling, sunset, and coastal views.

thingsToDo.title: Sunset Beach
thingsToDo.description: Visit the small city beach for an easy Gulf sunset or picnic away from the busier sponge district.

thingsToDo.title: Greek food and cultural heritage
thingsToDo.description: Make time for bakeries, seafood, Orthodox heritage, and the Greek-American community that transformed Tarpon Springs through the sponge industry.

thingsToDo.title: Anclote Key Preserve State Park
thingsToDo.description: Take a boat trip to the separate offshore state park for beaches, wildlife, and lighthouse views; it is not Tarpon Springs city parkland.

bestTimeToVisit.title: Cooler months are easiest for outdoor planning
bullets: Late fall through early spring generally brings lower humidity and comfortable outdoor conditions.
Summer is hot, humid, and storm-prone; start exposed activities early and keep afternoon plans flexible.
Busy winter and holiday periods reward advance reservations for popular tours and timed attractions.

faq.a: Two to three days is a good starting point for the core sights plus one outdoor or regional experience.

faq.a: Yes. The strongest itineraries combine the destination itself with nearby water, parks, preserves, or trails.

sections.heading: Overview
paragraphs: Tarpon Springs is an incorporated Gulf Coast city on the Anclote River in northern Pinellas County.

sections.heading: Geography & setting
paragraphs: River, bayous, Gulf shoreline, and offshore islands shaped the sponge fleet and continue to shape recreation.

sections.heading: History & culture
paragraphs: Greek immigrants and sponge divers created one of Florida's most distinctive local cultural landscapes in the early 20th century.

sections.heading: Outdoor & seasonal highlights
paragraphs: Boating, beaches, paddling, fishing, and offshore island trips complement the historic waterfront.

sections.heading: Getting around
paragraphs: The Sponge Docks and downtown are walkable clusters; a car or boat is needed for beaches and Anclote Key.
